summaryBox.takeaway: Arrhenius: H⁺/OH⁻ in water. Brønsted: proton donor/acceptor. Lewis: electron pair acceptor/donor.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CONJUGATE ACID-BASE PAIRS
                       
   HCl (a1) + H₂O (b2) ⇌ H₃O⁺ (a2) + Cl⁻ (b1)
   ├── Pair 1: HCl (Strong Acid) / Cl⁻ (Very Weak Conjugate Base)
   └── Pair 2: H₂O (Weak Base) / H₃O⁺ (Strong Conjugate Acid)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Arrhenius Theory**: Acid releases $\text{H}^+$ in water; Base releases $\text{OH}^-$ in water (valid strictly in aqueous systems).
• **Brønsted-Lowry Theory**: Acid is a **Proton ($\text{H}^+$) Donor**; Base is a **Proton ($\text{H}^+$) Acceptor**. Forms conjugate pairs (strong acid has weak conjugate base).
• **Lewis Theory**: Acid is an **Electron-Pair Acceptor** (Electrophile, e.g. $\text{BF}_3, \text{AlCl}_3, \text{Fe}^{3+}$); Base is an **Electron-Pair Donor** (Nucleophile, e.g. $\text{NH}_3, \text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{CN}^-$).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Ostwald’s Dilution Law for Weak Monoprotic Acids/Bases
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Ostwald’s Dilution Law for Weak Monoprotic Acids/Bases
conceptBreakdown.content:
Consider a weak acid $\text{HA}$ of initial concentration $C\text{ mol/L}$ with degree of ionization $\alpha$:
$$\text{HA}(aq) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+(aq) + \text{A}^-(aq)$$
$$K_a = \frac{[\text{H}^+][\text{A}^-]}{[\text{HA}]} = \frac{(C\alpha)(C\alpha)}{C(1-\alpha)} = \frac{C \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$$
For weak electrolytes where $\alpha \ll 1$ (typically $\alpha < 0.05$ or $5\%$):
$$1 - \alpha \approx 1 \implies K_a \approx C \alpha^2 \implies \mathbf{\alpha = \sqrt{\frac{K_a}{C}} = \sqrt{K_a \cdot V_m}}$$
$$\mathbf{[\text{H}^+] = C \alpha = \sqrt{K_a \cdot C}}$$
$$\mathbf{\text{pH} = \frac{1}{2} \left[ \text{p}K_a - \log_{10} C \right]}$$
• **Ostwald's Postulate**: The degree of ionization ($\alpha$) of a weak electrolyte is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar concentration ($C$) and directly proportional to the square root of dilution ($V_m$). As $C \to 0$ (infinite dilution), $\alpha \to 1.0$.

quickRevision: Conjugate pair differs by exactly one H⁺.
Lewis acids are electron pair acceptors; Lewis bases are electron pair donors.
